what_this_is: A REMOTE ARCHIVAL RETIREMENT of attempt75's nine C3 probe WEIGHTS. They have no byte-identical local copy -- the durable evidence directory holds 51 MiB of records and no safetensors -- so after this runs no copy of these weights exists anywhere. What survives is the binding record: every probe's identity, content hash, training config, run manifest, per-sample rows, scored aggregate and the canonical C3 verdict derived from them.
authorised_by: Maintainer decision, 2026-10-02, standing artifact/storage-lifecycle policy: do not preserve large historical checkpoints merely because they once existed. Retire the weights where the measurement/evaluation is valid and preserved, the artifact identity/hash is recorded, no downstream consumer needs the weight bytes, and reconstruction is unnecessary or adequately described -- preserving measurement, evaluation, manifests, hashes, configs, closeout, provenance and a tombstone. Decided under AGENTS.md P8.4.
why_now: NOT housekeeping: it is on A3's critical path. Account-wide private headroom was BISECTED at $0 with fresh random oids and sits between 12 and 13 GiB. A3's three probes need 6.664 GiB and fit; A3 plus one authorized retry needs 13.33 GiB and is REFUSED. The 2026-10-02 decision requires autonomous rerun of failed stages, and AGENTS.md P8.2.1 requires confirming a durable backend has room BEFORE a long experiment -- C1 attempt 18 lost six probes to exactly this and C3 attempt66 lost nine.
supersedes_rule: The sole-copy rule still stands for everything outside the set below. These nine objects are cleared by the consumer rule, not by copy count.
selection_rule: Exactly the nine attempt75 probe weight objects. Their small sidecars -- config.json and generation_config.json -- are NOT retired: they remain as reconstruction and accountability metadata. Nothing else was considered; the nine alone clear the requirement with margin, and over-deleting to a byte target is not authorized.
conditions_checked_per_object: COMPLETE AND VALIDLY SCORED -- attempt75 trained 9 of 9, preserved 9 of 9 and scored 9 of 9 on one protocol-uniform field (generation fingerprint c318d1c62197 across all nine), and the canonical C3 verdict NO_GO was derived from them on 2026-10-01

EVIDENCE DURABLE AND RECORDED -- per-sample rows, scored aggregates, generation files and training descriptors at /home/ecs-user/aad-artifacts/phase_c3/attempt75 (235 files, 19 classes), with c3_probe_results.json and c3_decision.json git-tracked under logs/stages/stage-1/phase_c3/analyses/attempt75_stage_i/, and each probe's result_sha256 and per_sample_sha256 recorded in this document

NO AUTHORIZED CONSUMER READS THE WEIGHTS -- audited 2026-10-02: no scripts/pod/autoinit_*_launch.py declares the prefix, no scripts/pod/*.sh fetches it, the checkpoint registry does not name it, and every code reference to attempt75 reads its committed EVIDENCE json. A3's own control loader (write_a_bsz3_adoption.controls_from_attempt75) reads c3_probe_results.json and consumes no bytes

NO UNSCORED OR RESUMABLE MEASUREMENT DEPENDS ON THEM -- all nine are scored, the C3 verdict is complete and terminal, and retrying, resuming or pooling that measurement is forbidden, so no authorized computation could consume these weights

RECONSTRUCTION IS ADEQUATELY DESCRIBED -- each arm rebuilds from the frozen shared parent eea90c91346a under its digest gate and each probe trains from the frozen recipe at its frozen seed; attempt75 reproduced attempt66's three arm identities exactly on fresh hardware, which is the evidence that the path is deterministic rather than the hope
NOT A PROTECTED CLASS, not a canonical release artifact, and not an irreplaceable lineage or input artifact

unreadable_launchers_reviewed._how_reviewed: RE-VERIFIED FROM SOURCE on 2026-10-02, not inherited from the 2026-09-30 record: the tree has moved since, so a previous review is evidence that the check was done once, not that its answer still holds. executed.method: HfApi.permanently_delete_lfs_files(rewrite_history=True), selected by exact file_oid identity, executed by scripts/autoinit/retire_relay_copies.py --archival-authorization ... --execute. Ordinary deletion reclaims nothing on this account -- measured twice -- because LFS is billed including history.
executed._the_tool_re_derived_everything: it refused the first invocation because two launchers could not build their specs, so their declared relay inputs were unknown. Both were then re-verified FROM SOURCE -- not inherited from the 2026-09-30 review -- and named in unreadable_launchers_reviewed. The dry run then reported 'plan == authorization (9 objects), nothing extra'.

quota_measured.method: bisected against the LFS batch endpoint with FRESH RANDOM oids. An oid that already exists dedups and returns a false PASS, so reusing a known oid would measure nothing.
quota_measured._why_this_is_measured_and_not_assumed: this repository has twice deleted objects and reclaimed nothing. The reclaim is a measurement, and the authorized retry path is executable because the endpoint says six probes fit, not because nine were deleted.

tombstone._this_document_is_the_tombstone: There is no local artifact to tombstone in checkpoint_tombstones.json: these objects were remote-only. This record is what outlives the bytes, and it carries per probe the arm, the seed, the probe id, the initialization artifact digest, the scored result sha256, the per-sample sha256 and the two headline rates.
